entities.summary:
Pietro Lombardo (1435–1515) was an Italian Renaissance sculptor and architect, born in Carona (Ticino), and the father of Tullio Lombardo and Antonio Lombardo. He is best known for his work on the tomb of Francesco Sforza in Milan, and his contributions to the development of Renaissance sculpture and architecture.

  Lombardo's work was characterized by its classical influences and its use of new materials and techniques, such as the use of terracotta and the development of the 'Lombardo style' of sculpture. He was also a prolific architect, designing buildings in Milan, Cremona, and other cities in northern Italy.

  Despite his significant contributions to the arts, Lombardo's legacy was largely overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries, such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo. However, his work continues to be studied and admired by art historians and enthusiasts today.

  The impact of Lombardo's work can be seen in the many Renaissance-style buildings and sculptures that continue to be found in Italy and other parts of Europe, and his influence can be seen in the work of many later artists and architects.

  Lombardo's own life was marked by both artistic and personal struggles, including a long and difficult relationship with his father, who was a blacksmith, and a period of exile in Cremona, where he continued to work on his art.

  Through his work, Lombardo helped to establish Milan as a major center of artistic and cultural production in northern Italy, and his legacy continues to be celebrated today.
